name: Skylab
tagline: America’s first space station hosted crews above Earth, then made an uncontrolled-looking but tracked farewell across the sky.
credit: Original editorial illustration created for the Left Behind archive.

beats.goal: Serve as America's first space station for long-duration human missions and scientific research in orbit.
beats.achieved: Three astronaut crews lived aboard Skylab, conducting experiments in astronomy, medicine, Earth observation, and space science while setting new records for time spent in space.
beats.ending: Without the Space Shuttle available to boost its orbit, Skylab gradually lost altitude because of atmospheric drag. It re-entered Earth's atmosphere on July 11, 1979, with most of it burning up and some debris falling into the Indian Ocean and Western Australia.
beats.now: Skylab no longer exists; it was destroyed during atmospheric re-entry.
beats.learned: The mission demonstrated the value of long-term human spaceflight and influenced the design and operation of later space stations such as the International Space Station.
